_comment: lentiMPRA (Agarwal et al. 2025), K562. Stage 2 = full fine-tuning of the encoder, no EMA.
Hyperparameters are a one-for-one mirror of the JAX run in
alphagenome_FT_MPRA/configs/mpra_K562.json, so the two implementations differ only in
framework. Unlike agarwal2025_fullft.json (tuned once on K562 and reused), these were
tuned per cell type on the JAX side, so batch size, hidden width, dropout and both
learning rates differ between the three.
Deliberate departures from agarwal2025_fullft.json, each to match JAX:
optim.optimizer adam (not adamw); lr_scheduler constant (JAX sets none);
early_stopping_patience 5 (JAX); head.first_layer_rank null (JAX has no low-rank
first layer); dropout and head width per cell.
Splits are the publication's folds (train 2-9, val 1, test 10), NOT the Malinois
chromosome holdout 1_train.py uses by default - pass --split_by fold.
NOTE: the published PyTorch K562 checkpoint does NOT use this head. It came from a
separate hyperparameter sweep and has a two-layer [2048, 1024] gelu head, where JAX
and this config use a single [2048] relu layer. HepG2 and WTC11 already match JAX.
